summary: Crow's nest on Ojibway Knoll (Kaniksu NF): built 1936 with a garage cabin, abandoned 1948; a later visit found two buried bed frames.

facts.design: Crow's nest, with a garage cabin an eighth of a mile to the west
facts.status_note: Crow's nest abandoned in 1948; no standing structure is described on the summit now. Willhite's photo captions list bed frames, a phone line and metal sheets.

visit.trail_note: About a quarter mile of hiking from the end of a rough road, then a bushwhack to the top; high-clearance vehicle advised (Willhite)

events.note: Crow's nest on the site, with a garage cabin 1/8 mile to the west
Crow's nest abandoned, per the register, the listing and Willhite

evidence.supports: lookout was a crow's nest; 1936; garage cabin 1/8 mile west
evidence.quote: There was a crow's nest on the site in 1936 along with a garage cabin 1/8 mile to the west.

evidence.supports: crow's nest 1936, garage cabin 1/8 mile west
evidence.quote: 1936: crow's nest, garage cabin 1/8 mile west. Abandoned 1948.
The Kresek inventory says there was a crows nest here in 1936, lasting until abandoned in 1948.

evidence.supports: Willhite thought the tree base might still be discoverable
evidence.quote: I would bet the base of the crows nest tree is still discoverable

evidence.supports: two bed frames, about 90 percent buried
evidence.quote: I found 2 bed frames 90 percent buried by earth

evidence.supports: open area on the south side of the summit
evidence.quote: The south side of the summit still has some open areas

evidence.supports: route starts at Usk on Kings Lake Road over the Pend Oreille River
evidence.quote: From Usk, take Kings Lake Road over the Pend Oreille River to an intersection.

evidence.supports: forest road FR50 up to the ridge
evidence.quote: follow FR50 up to the ridge

evidence.supports: steep rocky track to a saddle between two knobs
evidence.quote: Follow this steep rocky road, deteriorating in places, to its end inside the saddle between the two knobs of Ojibway.

evidence.supports: about a quarter mile of hiking

evidence.quote: Access: High-clearance best (1 extra mile if not)
you will need to turn right and bushwhack (pretty easy) up to the top.

evidence.supports: photo captions list a phone line

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the 1936 and 1948 dates come from one inventory (Kresek) repeated on three pages. The Willhite visit is undated. Record kind 'platform' fits 'crow's nest'. No source states the access status, so facts.access is left unset; the route and lack of any closure are described in the story. The record's access 'unknown' can stay until someone checks land status. The tree the crow's nest may have stood in is only hinted at by Willhite.
